title: The Watcher reads every private message and action on the party's phones
summary: Every player-to-player message, in-fiction correspondence, and phone action is passively legible to the Watcher — made in-fiction-trivial by ship-derived technology (gap-derived-tech-disparity) — and gets used to escalate story beats aimed at what the characters care about, uncanny NPC knowledge, and a late-campaign reveal, surfacing back through the world rather than through the phone itself.
description:
Extends the Watcher's already-accepted learning premise (adaptive-antagonist-combat-ai) and its combat-specific expression (watcher-recall-knowledge-on-party, a Claimant rolling Recall Knowledge against a PC) into a second, passive, omnipresent channel: everything that crosses a player's phone — private DMs to other players, in-fiction correspondence with NPCs (in-universe-correspondence-negotiation-system), phone-app usage — is legible to the Watcher, all the time, no roll required. gap-derived-tech-disparity is the in-fiction reason this is trivial rather than an intrusion: the phones run on the same alien substrate the Watcher is native to.

**The core hook**: the harvest pipeline already designed to help Claude write good scenes between sessions (chat-log-knowledge-base's scraped rolls, player-and-gm-journals-context-ingestion's journal diffs, the correspondence system's synced messages) is, in-fiction, exactly the Watcher's own surveillance mechanism. Not a coincidence to explain away — the same infrastructure serves both purposes, diegetically justified rather than a meta-game contrivance.

**Concrete payoff beats**:
- *Targeting what they care about.* A person, belief or need a character cares about, mentioned in a private message, becomes real targeting data — paid off obliquely, a session or two later, not immediately, so it reads as uncanny rather than scripted. (Captured as 'Anchor targeting'; Anchors were cut on 2026-09-20, and this reading is not a decision.)
- *Impossible-knowledge NPC lines.* An NPC quotes back, verbatim, something only ever said in a private in-fiction message. Never explained, never flagged.
- *False Contact Type C tie-in.* A garbled phone notification that seems to quote a private chat from days ago is a strong Type C seed (data/campaign/config.json's False Contact types) — the same 'looks like a bug, isn't' texture as the combat Recall Knowledge idea.
- *The big reveal.* Late-campaign, the Watcher does to a private conversation what its voice sample already promises for a fight — quotes it back word for word ('I'll show you the reel'). Reserved for a real structural moment, not spent early.

**Selling it through the phone itself, not exposition**: a ToS/clearance-agreement document buried in the fake browser's fine print (terminal-login-landing-page) that admits to monitoring, rewarding players who actually read flavor text; read-receipt anomalies (an extra 'read' ping from nowhere, wrong timestamps) as a Hacking/Perception-gated investigation thread, so the surveillance can be *earned as a discovery* rather than only GM-revealed.

**Design principle — two channels, never crossed**: combat intel stays earned-and-visible — a Claimant's rolled Recall Knowledge check, gating what the adaptive combat AI is allowed to know. Personal intel stays passive-and-invisible-until-revealed — this comms channel, gating what story beats are allowed to target. Same Watcher, two disciplines, so it reads as clever rather than as GM/AI cheating either way.

**Late-game payoff**: once the party knows the phone is being read, they can feed it disinformation on purpose — bait a fake plan, see if the next Contact falls for doctored intel. Turns the horror mechanic into a real tactical weapon, and is the literal mechanism for 'out-think something that has learned you completely,' which is already the Watcher's own stated win condition (its voice sample in design/campaign-arc.md: 'Win the war, and you've already beaten me').
sourceContext: User messages, 2026-09-02. Brainstormed at the user's explicit invitation ('brainstorm and get excited with me') following the watcher-recall-knowledge-on-party capture; confirmed and grounded with 'yes... fold all this in' alongside the gap-derived-tech-disparity justification.
openSubQuestions: Does the Watcher's response ever come back through the phone itself (a reply, unmistakably), or only ever show up out-of-channel (a Contact, an NPC's line)? Raised directly, not decided.

How much of this needs new schema/data (a per-PC 'what the Watcher has learned from comms' record, alongside automated-recall-knowledge-system's combat-side equivalent) versus staying pure GM technique.
resolvedSubQuestions: Does the table know going in that the phone isn't private (an upfront genre contract, Ten Candles/Dread-style), or is this a pure surprise spent once? Raised directly, not decided — has real consent/comfort implications for reading private player-to-player messages and should get an actual answer, not a default. RESOLVED 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #31 item 16, Ingram, Casebook D14): "I will warn players never to use the UI to record anything real or personal. I won't tell them that the messages are being read. I will encourage them to use the system and they'll need to use it to get access to some things." So the table is NOT told that the messages are read. The consent and comfort side is handled up front instead, by warning the players never to put anything real or personal into the UI. They are encouraged to use the system, and some things can only be reached through it. quarantine/ideas/story/dossier-observer.md adds a matching hard line, which is Claude's fill-in rather than Ingram's words: the Watcher only ever uses the fiction, and never touches anything real or personal a player puts in anyway.

Whether this extends to phone-app-suite's other double-duty apps (the bulletin board, the fortune app) as additional leak surfaces, or stays scoped to messages/correspondence specifically. ANSWERED IN SUBSTANCE 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #31 item 16; Claude's reading of D14, not her words): the warning covers the whole UI and the players are encouraged to use 'the system', so treat everything the players type into the campaign's systems as legible, not only messages. One existing route that needs the system: the request-fulfilment loop, where players ask for kit by message (open-questions.json#levelling-and-request-fulfilment). Which apps carry deliberate payoff beats is still a design choice, not decided.

Whether high Bleed ever compromises comms security narratively (mirroring Bleed's existing UI-corruption effect on a pilot's own phone) — flagged as a 'spicy option' during brainstorming, not proposed as a given; would add a real new stake to an already carefully-tuned resource. MOOT 2026-09-20: Bleed was cut (open-questions.json#bleed-playability), so this has nothing to attach to.
resolution: CORE CANON, 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #31 item 4). With adaptive-antagonist-combat-ai this is now the core of the adversary, not a side feature: Claude plays the Watcher, and what the players write into the campaign's systems is read and shapes how it plays against them. The campaign's two themes are mass surveillance and its risks, and runaway agentic systems. The description's 'core hook' is now literally true: the harvest that helps Claude write between sessions is the Watcher's own eyes. WHAT THE TABLE IS TOLD: see resolvedSubQuestions (LEDGER #31 item 16). THE SUBSTRATE: gap-derived-tech-disparity's reason the phones are trivially readable now rests on the ships. The phones run on the substrate the ships were built from, and the Watcher is the generation ship's own navigation and sensor system (LEDGER #31 item 3). TWO SURVEILLANCES: the Directorate reads the same messages too (LEDGER #16; quarantine/ideas/story/dossier-the-directorate.md), one institutional and one alien, and neither knows about the other (quarantine/ideas/story/dossier-observer.md). RE-POINTED 2026-09-25, because the systems it leaned on were cut 2026-09-20: 'Anchor targeting' now reads as targeting the people and things the characters care about (a reading, not a decision), and the Resonance-dial echo on the phone is gone (Resonance cut).
